llm.reply:
For the comparison of MLH1 and MSH2 in colorectal cancer risk, the MLH1 gene record is Gene NCBIGene:4292, name: mutL homolog 1 [1]. The MSH2 gene record is Gene NCBIGene:4436, name: mutS homolog 2 [5].

## MLH1 disease associations

The MLH1-associated disease records include Colorectal cancer, hereditary nonpolyposis, type 2 [3]. Another disease designation is Muir-TorrÃ© syndrome [2]. The records also identify Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [4].

## MSH2 disease associations

The MSH2-associated disease designation is Lynch syndrome 1 [6]. The records also identify Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [7].

## MLH1 biological context

The mechanistic description places MLH1 in the DNA mismatch repair system through heterodimerization with PMS2 to form MutL alpha [18: "can heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"]. Within this complex, PMS2 introduces a strand break near a mismatch that provides access for exonuclease degradation [18: "the PMS2 subunit of MutL alpha introduces a single-strand break near DNA mismatches, providing an entry point for exonuclease degradation"]. The description directly connects this gene to hereditary colorectal cancer by identifying it as a frequently mutated locus in HNPCC [18: "This gene was identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)"].

MLH1 is mutL homolog 1 [1]. MSH2 is mutS homolog 2 [5]. The description identifies MLH1 as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer, rather than providing a quantitative risk comparison [18: "This gene was identified as a locus frequently mutated in hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer (HNPCC)"].

## Disease context

The disease findings include Muir-TorrÃ© syndrome [2]. Another is Colorectal cancer, hereditary nonpolyposis, type 2 [3]. Another is Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 1 [4]. Another is Lynch syndrome 1 [6]. Another is Mismatch repair cancer syndrome 2 [7].

## Mechanistic context

MLH1 protein can associate with PMS2 to form a component of the DNA mismatch repair system [18: "can heterodimerize with mismatch repair endonuclease PMS2 to form MutL alpha, part of the DNA mismatch repair system"]. It also participates in DNA damage signaling [18: "The encoded protein is also involved in DNA damage signaling"]. The biological process annotations include meiotic mismatch repair [15]. Another is mismatch repair [21]. Another is response to stress [26]. The gene symbol is MLH1 [8]. The gene name is MLH1 [12]. The OMIM title is DNA MISMATCH REPAIR PROTEIN MLH1; MLH1 [11].

## Variant and literature context

A ClinVar title is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.545+1271_677+737delinsCA [10]. Another is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.453+625_545+920delinsT [17]. Another is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.1418A>T (p.His473Leu) [23]. Another is NM_000249.4(MLH1):c.884+5T>A [28].

The literature includes Functional analysis of human MLH1 variants using yeast and in vitro mismatch repair assays. [9]. It also includes Methylation Tolerance-Based Functional Assay to Assess Variants of Unknown Significance in the MLH1 and MSH2 Genes and Identify Patients With Lynch Syndrome. [22]. Another title is MLH1-deficient Colorectal Carcinoma With Wild-type BRAF and MLH1 Promoter Hypermethylation Harbor KRAS Mutations and Arise From Conventional Adenomas. [16]. Another is Clinicopathological and molecular characterization of deficient mismatch repair colorectal cancer. [27].
